note: Holdings-relevant market news, researched daily by the intel agent (multi-theme sweep: precious metals, HK tech, SGX/Singapore, rare earths, macro) with sources. The "actionable" line relates each item to this specific portfolio. Not financial advice.

items.headline: Silver down 25% in a month to $58 after breaking $62 support; analysts flag $52 as the next major level
items.summary: Silver traded at $58.24/oz on June 26, down 25.4% from $78.08 a month earlier after peaking above $121 earlier in 2026, and has now broken below the $62.00 support analysts flagged the prior week, leaving ~$52.00 as the next major support. The metal is still up 58.9% year-over-year and the structural ~67-million-ounce 2026 supply deficit remains intact, but the technical picture is firmly bearish near term.
items.actionable: This is the highest-risk item for the levered silver stack: check margin buffers immediately and consider trimming leverage or hedging while price still sits above the $52 support, since a break there compounds fast on a levered book.

items.headline: Warsh's first FOMC holds rates at 3.50-3.75% with hawkish tilt — nearly all policymakers see rates flat or higher through 2026
items.summary: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting ended with a unanimous hold at 3.50-3.75% and a stripped-down statement closing with 'The committee will deliver price stability,' which markets read as hawkish. The dot plot showed a 2026 median of 3.80% with all but one policymaker projecting rates flat or higher by year-end, against May CPI of 4.2% YoY on post-Iran-conflict energy prices.
items.actionable: The removal of the rate-cut tailwind is the root cause of the metals drawdown, so keep the ~60% cash earning short rates and stage any re-entry into silver/miners in tranches only after the July 28-29 FOMC clarifies the path.

items.headline: May core PCE hits 3.4% YoY, hottest since October 2023; headline 4.1% — a Q4 Fed hike is now roughly fully priced
items.summary: The BEA's May Personal Income and Outlays report showed headline PCE up 4.1% YoY (largely energy-driven after the Iran conflict) and core PCE up 3.4% YoY (0.3% m/m), the highest core reading since October 2023. It landed a week after the June FOMC, where nine of 19 officials projected at least one 25bp hike this year, and markets now price a Q4 hike as roughly fully done.
items.actionable: With a hike fully priced and core inflation still accelerating, avoid averaging down into levered silver, expect some cap-rate pressure on SGX REITs, and keep the cash bucket in short-dated instruments earning the higher-for-longer yield.

items.headline: Gold breaks below $4,000 as hawkish Fed and Middle East peace strip out the safe-haven bid
items.summary: On June 23 gold futures fell 1.3% to $4,149.40 and silver dropped more than 5% to $62.07/oz; by June 24 gold traded below $4,000 for the first time in months, and by June 26 it sat near $4,066, down 11.6% from its June 1 open. The selloff was driven by the hawkish June FOMC, a dollar at a one-year peak, and the fading geopolitical premium after the US-Iran framework.
items.actionable: Levered metal exposure suffers compounding decay in a downtrend, so cutting leverage or buying puts on the silver/miner sleeve beats averaging down until either hike odds or the dollar rally break.

items.headline: US and Iran sign framework to end the war; Brent drops below $80 to three-month lows as Strait of Hormuz reopens
items.summary: The US and Iran signed a memorandum of understanding extending the ceasefire 60 days and reopening the Strait of Hormuz to all shipping, with reports the US will allow Iran to sell oil immediately. Brent fell about 5% to close below $80 (as low as ~$78.24, lowest since early March), WTI settled near $76, and equities rallied on the de-escalation.
items.actionable: The bleeding war premium is bearish for the silver/gold-miner sleeve but a tailwind for HK tech and SGX REITs via cheaper energy and risk-on flows — do not count on a safe-haven bid returning to metals near term.

items.headline: Hang Seng closes out worst week in over a year as renewed sell-off engulfs tech names
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index fell 1.8% on June 26 to 22,671.86, capping a 5.2% weekly loss — its biggest since April 2025 — with the Hang Seng Tech Index down 3.4% on the day. The rout was attributed to the Fed's hawkish pivot, unwinding of leveraged AI bets across Asia (Kospi fell as much as 9% intraday), doubts over AI monetisation, and fragile China consumer confidence plus regulatory scrutiny of platform subsidies.
items.actionable: Expect continued volatility in the Tencent/SMIC/Xiaomi sleeve and stagger any adds from cash rather than buying the first bounce, since the drawdown is macro-driven rather than company-specific.

items.headline: Gold ETFs snap four-week, $7.6B outflow streak with $1.1B inflow; Goldman cuts year-end target to $4,900
items.summary: Physical gold-backed ETFs attracted 5.1 tonnes (~$1.1 billion) in the week ending mid-June, the largest weekly inflow since April, reversing four straight weeks of redemptions totaling 58.2 tonnes (~$7.6 billion); total holdings stand at 4,086.3 tonnes. Goldman Sachs simultaneously lowered its year-end 2026 gold target to $4,900/oz from $5,400, citing Fed rate-hike risk and easing geopolitical tensions.
items.actionable: Dip-buyers re-engaging around $4,000 gold supports holding the GDX/SLVP core, but Goldman's target cut argues against adding aggressively before the July FOMC clarifies the rate path.

items.headline: Tencent and Xiaomi keep buying back shares through the sell-off; Tencent spends HK$501m per session
items.summary: HKEX filings show Tencent repurchased 1.186 million shares for HK$501 million on June 25 (at HK$418.2-428.6), after buying another HK$501 million worth on June 23. Cumulative repurchases under the current mandate reached 28.65 million shares, about 0.314% of issued capital, and Xiaomi also conducted buybacks on both days.
items.actionable: Consistent HK$500m/day buybacks into weakness provide a price floor and signal management confidence, supporting holding Tencent and Xiaomi through the drawdown rather than de-risking at these levels.

items.headline: Singapore May core inflation holds at 1.4%, below forecasts; MAS/MTI keep 2026 outlook at 1.5-2.5%
items.summary: A joint MAS/MTI statement showed core inflation steady at 1.4% y/y in May, below the 1.6% consensus, with headline inflation unchanged at 1.8%; both agencies maintained their 2026 forecasts at 1.5-2.5%. The soft print lands with 3M compounded SORA already down to roughly 1.07%, near multi-year lows.
items.actionable: Benign inflation plus ~1% SORA is a direct tailwind for the SGX REIT and developer sleeve via cheaper refinancing and DPU support — hold or add on dips rather than rotating that sleeve into low-yielding SGD cash.

items.headline: SGD slips to near 2026 lows as USD/SGD tests 1.30; OCBC sees less urgency for MAS tightening at July review
items.summary: OCBC FX research noted USD/SGD at about 1.2970, near the top of its 2026 range with resistance at 1.2980-1.3030, driven by broad USD strength and softer risk sentiment from the tech/AI sell-off. Its economists said the below-forecast May CPI leaves less urgency for MAS to tighten at the July MPC, after MAS steepened the S$NEER appreciation slope to 1% in April.
items.actionable: A softer SGD flatters DBS's USD earnings but erodes the USD value of the large SGD cash pile, and the same broad-USD strength is a near-term headwind for the levered silver and miner positions — avoid adding leverage there until the USD move stalls near 1.30.

items.headline: Pentagon inks $1.2 billion in rare-earth loans — $725M to Energy Fuels, $500M to Phoenix Tailings — as UUUU also buys magnet maker VAC for $1.9B
items.summary: The DoD Office of Strategic Capital signed a $725 million, 20-year conditional loan commitment with Energy Fuels on June 18 to expand rare-earth processing at White Mesa Mill (UUUU rallied ~9%), days after a $500 million conditional loan to Phoenix Tailings for a separation and metallization plant targeting 2028 operations. On June 23 Energy Fuels separately agreed to acquire German magnet maker Vacuumschmelze for ~$1.9 billion ($718M cash plus 65.85M new shares, closing early 2027), which would make it the first Western company integrated from mining to finished NdFeB magnets.
items.actionable: Washington is putting a financing floor under Western rare-earth economics, so a starter position in UUUU or MP funded from cash is reasonable — but note UUUU's large VAC share issuance creates a dilution/integration overhang worth letting settle first.

items.headline: China blacklists MP Materials and USA Rare Earth among 10 US firms, then adds whistleblower hotline to tighten export enforcement
items.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce added 10 US companies — including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth plus defense firms — to its export control list effective June 22, barring Chinese exporters and third-party re-exporters from supplying them with dual-use items, in retaliation for the Pentagon's expansion of its Chinese Military Companies list; MP fell 13.4% over June. On June 24 MOFCOM also launched a whistleblower hotline (effective July 1) rewarding tips on unauthorized strategic-mineral exports and transshipment, signaling aggressive enforcement of the export-control regime.
items.actionable: Escalating Chinese restrictions raise the scarcity premium on ex-China supply and validate the Western onshoring thesis, so treat MP/USAR headline dips as potential scale-in points for the watchlist while noting marginal supply-chain risk for hardware-exposed Xiaomi.
